title: The memoized per-part revision proof, frozen: 26% of an opened PPTX lifecycle, a durable format bump, and one selector made slower
decision: retained, design only; no production change
code_state: docs/performance only; no file under crates/ or tools/ is modified on the branch. The scratch implementation used for sizing is retained as patches in the evidence packet and exists nowhere else.
reason_codes: change 0590 declined part (c) of PPTX-1 because package_fingerprint is serialized into the durable LPRM0001 and LPCP0002 headers, so redefining it is a wire-format change that needs a frozen design first; this is that record

the design is a two-tier proof: a memoized payload digest keyed by blob Arc identity and length, and a per-part digest over the name, content type, payload digest and relationships, with the revision a hash over the sorted per-part digests under litchi-pptx-opened-v2

the payload tier is separate on purpose: content type and relationships are not behind the blob Arc, so memoizing the whole per-part digest on that key would return a stale digest for a part whose relationships changed

the retained Arc in the memo is load-bearing rather than an optimization: without it the (address, length) key is an ABA hazard, because a freed payload's address can be recycled by a different payload
Part is a public trait and blob_arc() need not agree with blob(); the memo applies the same alias test litchi-opc already applies at package.rs:435 and declines to memoize any part that fails it

verdicts are preserved: the proof is a function of exactly the v1 input tuple, the new encoding is injective, the part order is canonical, and every in-crate verdict is R(A)==R(B) for two packages in the same build — so a valid application applies, a stale one conflicts identically, and an exact no-op still compares equal
the cost of tiering is quantified rather than elided: R2 offers 2k+1 hash instances to collide instead of one, about 9 bits of the 128-bit generic margin at k=256

sized by a scratch implementation on change 0590's four retained selectors: an eager lifecycle falls 26.15% in instructions, and the fingerprint subtree falls 74.33%, which confirms 0590's modelled 2.5 G Ir / 23% estimate at 2.735 G Ir / 26.15%

the design needs the facade carry to be worth landing: a Snapshot-only memo is -8.63%, the facade-carried memo is -26.15%, because the two remaining fingerprints belong to Package::apply_opened_presentation_patch, the public durable-patch route, which holds no snapshot

accepted_evidence.counts: callgrind isolation pairs at --warmup 0 --samples 1 and 3, differenced over the two extra samples, per leg (before, scratch A, scratch A+B) for pptx_eager_batch_edit_save, pptx_eager_multi_slide_batch_edit_save, pptx_slide_move_boundary_save and pptx_slide_remove_boundary_save; whole-sample totals plus inclusive Ir for the fingerprint subtree and sha2::sha256::compress256
accepted_evidence.call_site_split: inclusive Ir per (caller, callee) pair from the callgrind out files, separating capture_internal's cold fingerprint from Transaction::commit's memoized one
accepted_evidence.memo_hit_rate: a probe build with per-fingerprint hit/miss and bytes-fed counters, run once on pptx_eager_batch_edit_save; 228 of 229 parts hit, 3,499 payload bytes hashed against 17,568,429, 93,763 bytes fed against 17,668,953
accepted_evidence.memo_resident_bytes: HashMap::capacity accounting at 29, 85 and 221 parts (3,192 / 6,384 / 12,768 bytes)
accepted_evidence.timing: tools/perf-baseline, --warmup 3 --samples 30, order A1 B1 B2 A2 on CPU 20, before against scratch A+B, with the A/A and B/B floors taken from the repeated legs in the same window
accepted_evidence.native_counters: perf stat -e cycles,instructions,task-clock around the same four legs
accepted_evidence.verdict_identity: a pairwise oracle over an 11-package corpus (base, byte-identical re-allocation, nine single-input mutations including a payload transposition): all 121 ordered pairs agree between packages_equal, the v1 revision and the v2 revision
accepted_evidence.suite: cargo test -p litchi-pptx 874 passed 0 failed and cargo test -p litchi --features docx,xlsx,pptx,xls 266 passed 0 failed, with the scratch implementation in place and the capture debug_assert re-deriving every reused revision

accepted_costs.durable_format: LPRM0001 -> LPRM0002 and LPCP0002 -> LPCP0003. Every previously serialized patch of both formats stops applying and must be re-planned; there is no migration and no dual read, because the public revision accessors are untyped [u8; 32] and two algebras behind one type would produce a silent false conflict
accepted_costs.error_identity: an input that used to parse now returns a new typed Error::DurablePatchRevisionFormat from from_bytes. Error is #[non_exhaustive] so the variant is additive, but the error identity of exactly the previously-accepted inputs moves
accepted_costs.per_part_tier: two extra SHA-256 initialize/finalize pairs and one hash-map insert per part per fingerprint: +3,100,432 Ir per cold fingerprint of the 229-part eager deck (+0.39%), +305,752 Ir per fingerprint of the 25-member boundary deck, about 13,539 Ir per part
accepted_costs.regression: pptx_slide_remove_boundary_save issues nine fingerprints per lifecycle and reuses none, so it pays the tier for nothing: +2.41% (A) and +2.45% (A+B) in callgrind instructions per lifecycle, +0.32% native instructions, +0.43% cycles against a -0.85% A/A floor
accepted_costs.memory: about 57 bytes per part of resident table per snapshot (13 KiB for a 229-part deck), plus one Arc refcount per memoized payload; the retention invariant keeps that at zero extra bytes only while it holds
accepted_costs.ambient_state: the facade carry (part B) puts a memo field on the mutable Package, refreshed at every opened-presentation publication. A stale memo can only miss, never answer wrongly, but between a non-publishing mutation and the next publication it can pin payloads the package has dropped
accepted_costs.collision_margin: the tiering offers 2k+1 hash instances instead of one, about 9 bits of the generic 128-bit collision margin at the default max_parts of 256

known_gaps.no_bump_in_the_scratch: the scratch implementation does not bump either magic and does not carry the typed refusal, so no measurement here says how an old-format patch behaves; admission gate 1 covers it
known_gaps.callgrind_pricing: callgrind runs SHA-256 in software and counts rep movsb per byte, so the 26.15% instruction figure is 2.31-2.45% in native instructions and 4.58-4.93% in cycles
known_gaps.noisy_window: the two boundary selectors ran in a window whose own floors (B/B p50 -10.17% on the move selector, A/A p50 -2.14% on the remove selector) are as wide as the effect; their counts are the result and their wall clock is not
known_gaps.memoized_fingerprint_cost: the about 7.3 M Ir cost of a memoized fingerprint is derived from the measured per-call-site split and the measured per-cold-fingerprint overhead, not measured in isolation
known_gaps.corpus_reach: no real-producer .pptx was measured; the mutation corpus is synthetic and the admission list requires the pairwise oracle to be extended over test-data/
known_gaps.unmeasured: no allocation-count, RSS, cold-cache, range-source, concurrency or cross-platform measurement; the memo's resident cost comes from HashMap::capacity rather than an allocator counter

withheld: any registered speedup, throughput, cold-cache, physical-I/O, range-source, concurrency-scaling, real-producer or cross-platform result
any statement that this design should land: it is frozen behind nine admission gates
